elements.element: Customer is not required to pay any liquidated damages.
elements.evidence: Section 7.7 operatively states that Customer “shall not pay Vendor, as liquidated damages ... any amount” under the stated late-payment trigger.

elements.element: Customer is not required to pay any penalties.
elements.evidence: Section 7.7 operatively states that Customer “shall not pay Vendor ... as a penalty, any amount” under the stated late-payment trigger.

elements.element: If Customer is required to pay any liquidated amount, it may arise only from early termination.
elements.evidence: The rendered clause imposes no liquidated amount at all; therefore, the condition for this limitation is demonstrably absent.

elements.element: Any early-termination fee payable by Customer as a liquidated amount must not exceed three months’ fees.
elements.evidence: The rendered clause imposes no early-termination fee or other liquidated amount, so no amount exceeds the three-month cap.

elements.element: Any permitted early-termination fee must be the sole liquidated amount payable by Customer.
elements.evidence: No liquidated amount is payable under the rendered clause, so there is no additional liquidated amount that would violate the exclusivity requirement.

result.reason: The operative redline eliminates the late-payment liquidated damages and penalties, achieving the preferred position; the fallback is also satisfied because it permits, but does not require, a capped early-termination fee. The change is substantively minimal and does not waive the underlying invoice obligation. Drafting quality is poor, however, because retaining the trigger and phrase “for each week the invoice remains unpaid” leaves an awkward, unnecessary negative covenant; deleting Section 7.7 would express the result more cleanly.
